findings.title: Team permission check requires admin AND owner instead of OR
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `await isTeamAdmin(...) && await isTeamOwner(...)`. A user who is a team admin but not an owner (or vice versa) will get false and be denied unless they are also the organizer/attendee. The consequence is legitimate team admins cannot add guests while the intent was admin-or-owner access.

findings.title: Original guests list sent to email sender instead of filtered list
findings.body: The handler filters `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (removing existing attendees and blacklisted emails) for DB creation, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the unfiltered input. Existing/blacklisted addresses that were not created will be treated as new guests inside sendAddGuestsEmails and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, sending wrong content to wrong people.

findings.title: Calendar update uses requester's credentials instead of organizer's
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts credentials are loaded with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and EventManager is built from `...user` where user is the caller. When the caller is an attendee or team admin rather than the booking owner, the calendar update runs with the wrong user's OAuth credentials/calendars. The consequence is updateCalendarAttendees fails or mutates the wrong calendar while the DB was already updated.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and bypassable
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts blacklisted emails are lowercased but compared as `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, and existing-attendee comparison is `guest === attendee.email`. An attacker can bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS with different casing (e.g. Blocked@x.com vs blocked@x.com) and create duplicate attendees differing only by case, defeating the blocklist and uniqueness intent.

findings.title: DB write committed before calendar update with no rollback
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts `prisma.booking.update` with `createMany` executes before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. If the calendar call throws, the function throws after guests are already persisted, leaving DB and calendar/email out of sync. A client retry will then fail with emails_must_be_unique_valid because the guests now exist, with no way to recover atomically.

findings.title: Unbounded guests array enables spam and DoS
findings.body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no max length, uniqueness, or normalization. Combined with per-attendee getTranslation and per-attendee email sending in the handler, a caller authorized as attendee/organizer can submit hundreds of arbitrary addresses in one call, creating many Attendee rows and triggering mass outbound emails. This is a spam and resource-exhaustion vector that needs a limit and dedup.

findings.title: Validation error flag never cleared on retry
findings.body: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx handleAdd sets `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` on failed validation but never sets it back to false when validation later succeeds. Once shown, the emails_must_be_unique_valid error persists even after the user fixes the emails, confusing users into thinking input is still invalid.

findings.title: Unsafe attendees[0] access can crash email rendering
findings.body: In organizer-add-guests-email.ts the subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` with no guard. If a booking has zero attendees the property access throws TypeError inside getNodeMailerPayload. Because the handler already persisted the new attendees before sending mail, this crash leaves the booking updated but emails unsent while the API still reports success due to swallowed email errors.
